ConnectionsView.pipelineAuthorizeDetail: You grant access through the provider's own consent screen, or a scoped API key you create and can revoke at any time. Aval never sees or stores your password, only a token or key limited to exactly the permissions listed for that connection.
ConnectionsView.pipelineNormalizeDetail: Every provider describes tenants, leases, and transactions differently. Aval maps each one into a single internal model, so the same report or automation works the same way whether the source is QuickBooks or CONTPAQi, AppFolio or Buildium.
ConnectionsView.pipelineReadModelsDetail: Normalized data is stored with its original source IDs and timestamps intact, so every number Aval shows you can be traced back to the exact upstream record it came from. Revoke a connection and Aval stops syncing immediately.
ConnectionsView.pipelineVerifyDetail: Before a connection is marked live, Aval calls the provider's own identity endpoint, confirming the actual QuickBooks company or WhatsApp phone number behind the credentials, so a typo or a stale key can't silently pass as working.
ConnectionsView.propertySystemsBody: Beyond the two required upstream systems, Aval can normalize data from any of these property management platforms.
ConnectionsView.tenantIsolatedCredentialsLeastPrivilegeS: Tenant-isolated credentials, least privilege, signed events, full revocation.

Independence.title: Independence
Independence.howConnect: Choose your language and region, then tell Aval which apps you use. Connect a source in Connections when you are ready.
Independence.howAsk: Open chat, choose an agent, and describe the outcome you want. Aval reads available evidence and proposes the next steps.
Independence.howReview: Follow progress in Tasks and review requests in chat or the Review Center. Find the module tour and independence examples in Settings → Preferences.
Independence.limits: Independence applies to your actions in this workspace. Agent permissions still apply. Sensitive actions need approval, and missing evidence or an unconfirmed provider result stops execution. Switching modes affects future actions; it cannot undo work already executed.

modes.supervised: Aval investigates; you approve each action before it runs.
modes.assisted: Aval proposes an exact plan; you approve it once, then Aval carries it out. Changed actions need new approval.
modes.autonomous: Aval carries out routine permitted work and reports results. Sensitive actions still need approval.

Independence.bootDescription: Choose how Aval should work with you. This choice is shared by Setup, chat, and your agent tasks in this workspace.

Independence.fixtureDescription: A resident reported a leaking tap. The sample work order is open and the maintenance channel is available. Aval proposes an acknowledgment and a follow-up.
Independence.fixtureDestination: Destination: synthetic maintenance outbox. No real recipient.

Independence.labLimits: This isolated rehearsal uses Aval’s actual routing and permission rules with scripted decisions and a temporary sample outbox. It does not call an AI model, connect a provider, or change workspace records. Changing mode or agent resets the rehearsal. It does not certify live provider delivery. Choosing a test agent does not change your workspace default.

overview.title: Portfolio overview
overview.body: Start with portfolio performance and recent workspace activity. Figures reflect the records available to Aval; connect or import data to fill gaps.

setup.title: Setup & independence
setup.body: Choose your default specialist, set how independently Aval works, and try the animated examples or synthetic rehearsal. Teach Aval the preferences you want it to remember.

tasks.title: Aval Tasks
tasks.body: Give an agent a concrete goal and follow its plan, evidence, checks, and results. Durable tasks keep their progress when you leave this screen.

reviewCenter.title: Review Center
reviewCenter.body: Review the exact content and destination of proposed actions. Yes approves that proposal; No rejects it. Sensitive actions retain their approval requirements in every mode.

inbox.title: Shared inbox
inbox.body: Read connected conversations and coordinate replies in one place. Channel availability depends on verified connections and their supported capabilities.

properties.title: Properties
properties.body: Keep the portfolio’s properties and units organized. This is the foundation for occupancy, leasing, and operating analysis.

leasing.title: Leasing
leasing.body: Follow available units and the path from an inquiry to a lease. Use the connected evidence to understand where the process needs attention.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.body: Review work orders, aging, and service performance. Ask the maintenance specialist to investigate an issue and propose a supported next step.

accounting.title: Accounting
accounting.body: Review financial records, receivables, and operating results. Aval uses source records for figures; selecting Autonomous does not enable unsupported money movement.

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure
infrastructure.body: Track meters, utility usage, and supporting bills. Use this module to connect resource consumption with the buildings you manage.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.body: See scheduled workspace activity and upcoming dates. Coordinate timing without losing the context of your operations.

projects.title: Projects
projects.body: Organize work into projects with clear ownership and progress. Use projects to keep larger operational efforts easy to follow.

teams.title: Teams
teams.body: Organize the people working together in your workspace. Team structure and workspace access help keep responsibilities clear.

connections.title: Connections
connections.body: Connect the apps that hold your records and conversations. Each app shows its actual readiness; a saved credential or catalog listing alone does not prove a working integration.

documents.title: Documents
documents.body: Bring documents into Aval and ask questions grounded in their contents. A document’s statements remain attributed to that source.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Manage your account, appearance, model connections, and onboarding preferences. Return here to update your language, region, or selected apps.

chat.title: Chat with Aval
chat.body: Ask questions or choose Start agent task for work that needs execution. Task progress and Yes/No approval requests now appear in chat; full traces remain in Tasks.

PmsSeat.title: Aval seat
PmsSeat.description: An address of your own that your property management system can mail, exactly as it would any employee. No API, no integration: your PMS sends, Aval receives. Because anyone can write to a public address, only senders you allow are ever read.
PmsSeat.loadError: Could not load the Aval seat.
PmsSeat.storageUnavailable: The seat is unavailable for this workspace.
PmsSeat.addressInstruction: Add this as a user in your PMS, or copy it on outbound notifications.
PmsSeat.noAddressYet: This workspace does not have a seat address yet.
PmsSeat.slugPermanent: This address is permanent. Once your PMS is sending to it, it cannot be reissued to anyone else — renaming later adds a second address and keeps this one working.
PmsSeat.sendersHeading: Senders allowed to write to your seat
PmsSeat.sendersExplanation: Mail is only read if it is cryptographically authenticated as coming from one of these domains. Subdomains are covered, so appfolio.com also allows mail.appfolio.com.
PmsSeat.noSenders: No sender is allowed yet, so nothing sent to your seat is being read.
PmsSeat.providerChanged: {domain} will now be read as a different system.
PmsSeat.suggestionsCaveat: Suggestions come from what each vendor publishes, not from mail Aval has seen. Large PMS deployments often send under your own domain instead — if what arrives is held below, allow that domain.
PmsSeat.unauthenticated: {count, plural, one {# message was} other {# messages were}} held from senders that could not be authenticated at all. They are not listed: the only sender name such a message carries is the one whoever sent it typed.
PmsSeat.verifiedCount: {count, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} verified and passed to Aval.
PmsSeat.sweepDelay: Allowing a sender also releases the mail already waiting from it, within about five minutes.
PmsSeat.ownerOnly: Only the workspace owner can change the seat address or its allowed senders.
